findings.title: The `/fruits/:id` fixture always returns fruit 1, so `find('fruit', 2)` tests the wrong record
findings.description: The handler sets `const fruit = fruits[0];` and ignores the `:id` parameter. The updated `find embedded` test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` (banana, `color_ids: [3]`) but asserts colors `[1, 2]`, which are apple's colors. The test only passes because the fixture ignores the id.

findings.title: Host lookup compares a lowercased column against a non-lowercased input
findings.description: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but `host` is `uri.host` and is never downcased. A referer such as `HTTP://EviltRout.com/page` yields `EviltRout.com`, which does not match the stored `eviltrout.com`, so the request is rejected. The fix is to downcase the input before the query.

findings.title: `before_validation` crashes when `host` is nil
findings.description: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called without a nil guard. Building or validating a record with no `host` raises `NoMethodError` instead of producing a validation error. `save_host` in `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` passes `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` straight through, so a request missing that field hits this path.

findings.title: Fabricator contents are swapped between the two files
findings.description: The file named `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now holds the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` holds only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The category fabricators were moved out of their file and the new file was given the wrong content.

findings.title: The embedding `update` action persists nothing
findings.description: `update` only calls `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`. A PUT to `customize/embedding` returns success without reading `params` or saving any hosts, so the route advertises an update that does not happen.

findings.title: Migration assumes an `embed_category` row exists and builds SQL by string interpolation
findings.description: The first query reads `execute(...)[0]['id']`, which raises `NoMethodError` when no `embed_category` setting matches a category. Each legacy host is interpolated directly into `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, so any value containing a quote breaks the statement or allows injection. Parameterised inserts or escaping would avoid both problems.

findings.title: `replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.description: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence. Any future type with two or more underscores will not match `ADMIN_MODELS`. Using a global regex (`/_/g`) would cover all cases. No current type in the list is affected.

findings.title: `pluralize` on the store is used without confirmation that it exists
findings.description: `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` depends on a `pluralize` method on the store. I could not confirm from the diff that it exists. Also, `hydrated || []` is dead code, because `Array.prototype.map` always returns an array, which is truthy.

findings.title: Describe block name typo: "emeddable"
findings.description: The context is titled `'with an emeddable host'`. The spelling should be "embeddable".

findings.title: Spec describe block still names the removed method
findings.description: The block is titled `"allows_embeddable_host"`, but the method under test is now `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`. The name no longer matches the code it exercises.
